## The single weakest link (judgement of this task)

**U3/U5b: the deployed sink.ts, the only component that writes committed state.** It is not only unproved; it is known to be wrong: a machine-checked counterexample (U5r-CONTRAST) and Node runs show that it commits two intents with one request id and does not bind the intent charge id, and every differential control pair with the real sink diverges (heavy/v4-1: exit 3 or 1). The night moved the repair forward only as DRAFTS: T-TOP composes the byte-level lemma up to the issuer method; the v4 draft sink (T-SHELLV4, U5v4-DIFF) removes the quadratic cost and binds the initial charge id, but its TypeScript loop is only tested (TS-LOOP-IS-FOLD), it depends on A-DB1..A-DB3, the review r-repairs found that its audit is structural only (a hostile balance reset gives a second refund: T-V4-ATTACK), and it still rests on NO-ROLLBACK, AUTHENTIC-INIT and DB-NO-FOREIGN-WRITER, which no audit over the database can check. The adoption diff (ADOPT-DIFF) applies and passes the Slice 1 suite, but is NOT applied. Runner-up: ADMISSION (S1, E1-E6): main is not protected and the gate admits run-time halts.
